The Father

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Exclusive: A father refuses to let justice slide after his daughter's rape. He goes after the perpetrator himself. Not only does he catch him but turns out he's a serial rapist.

Unique Selling Point:
We have the story exclusively. The father will speak, and in a TV first in SA, we are going to hide his identity using make up - a prosthetic nose and beard. This will ensure we meet the legal requirements. Dario has approved of this, as has Luke Lamrecht - in terms of the ethics.

SHOULD WE CONFRONT THE FATHER OF THE PERPETRATOR? I'LL LEAVE IT UP TO OFFICE. But he is SUUUUUUPER DANGEROUS. I'm happy to, William is happy to, Police say he's very dangerous, and has made witnesses and others disappear. He is also a convicted murderer.

STORY:
William is a father who has gone all out to catch the man who raped his daughter. He moved to South Africa from Malawi in 1997 and met his wife, who is South African, they have had two girls, Julia and Ennelise - "Nana" as a nickname.

When they lived in Muldersdrift, Nana was 11 years old, when a man in a taxi approached her. He wanted her to buy him a cigarette at the tuckshop. She complied. When she came back, he scooped her up onto his lap, and drove away with her. He took her past Lanseria airport and raped her brutally. The man then dropped her off in the bush, throwing a R20 note at her.

Hardly able to walk from the pain, she managed to get to the side of the road where another taxi managed to pick her up and drop her nearby her home. Her mother, and aunt immediately took her to a hospital, where they got a rape kit and J88 form done...and then they went through the painful process of her identifying her rapist and retelling the horror story. She was able to give a very good description, and semen was taken and sent for a DNA test. Then her mother called William, he was beside himself with grief. He couldn't believe this had happened, and he decided that no matter what he would get the man. Based on the description, William managed to track down the man who raped her - Tshepo Moeketsi. Turns out, he was a man well known to the community, not only that, but when they went to the Muldersdrift police station seems that there were several other cases of rape against him. However, he'd not been arrested. William insisted. The next thing, Tshepo's father called. A man also well known in the community - he had murdered a 12 year old boy who stole sweets from his tuckshop... he'd spent several years in jail for that crime. Tshepo's father came to William's house to ask if they could remunerate him (admitting his son was guilty) instead of him laying a charge. William said he must bring Tshepo to his house. But instead Tshepo went into hiding, as William had no intention of taking the bribe. William works as a chef and driver for Anthony Roux. Roux was devastated for William and helped him with the hospital bills, as Nana needed an operation after the ordeal. He also hired a PI to help William find the culprit. But the Muldersdrift police tipped off Tshepo's father, who hid Tshepo when the police raided the family home. And Tshepo remained hidden for the next 8 months.

William said he had sleepless nights, taking care of Nana, she was in a bad way. She had counselling which her mother took her to in Krugersdorp. But for a long time she couldn't sit, or go to the loo she was in such pain. She also had nightmares. William said it drove him to obsession. So he decided he would do everything to hunt down Tshepo.


Summary:
Meanwhile, William refused to drop the case, and Tshepo's father sent people to the family's house to threaten them and intimidate them. Roux moved William to a new house in cosmos city away from Muldersdrift as he worried for Williams family's safety. He then decided to help fund William's search for justice, giving him time off and money to go find Tshepo.

William began paying informers in the local townships, they would track William's father's vehicle, this lead to several other houses they owned, eventually going to one in a township called Madidi (which is near Brits). There William and two of his friends managed to find someone who knew Tshepo and confirmed Tshepo was staying in his father's house. They went from Tavern to Tavern to Tavern... until finally they found Tshepo... they followed him to his house... there they surprised him and found him hiding in the cupboard. William Tasered him, and it took everything in him to do the right thing. He took him to the police station, and finally Tshepo was arrested. When they got Tshepo's DNA back, turns out there were many rapes he was connected to. 16 woman, and 4 children. These are those that we know of.

Over the next year William went to every court hearing, some families were paid R50,000 to drop cases against Tshepo by his father, but William stayed the course - refusing to have his daughter "bought off". He gathered community members and got people to go to the court case - all the time Roux assisted where he could.

Finally last week Tuesday 28 July Tshepo, who was found guilty earlier this year, was sentenced to life in prison.

I told William about the law requiring us to conceal the identity of the child and family, and he said he and his wife want to speak, they dont need to have their real names, but they want to show their faces - they are adamant that he was able to rape their child because so many stayed silent or were happy to be paid off.


Further information:
There is some footage of the original raid of the police, a shaky cell phone video. But we have pictures of Tshepo's ID, and William can take us everywhere and show us what happened there. I think if we add this to the recent crime statistics, we can actually tell a positive story on a very dark tale. That's my idea - to do re-enactments and go to the places, and Tshepo tell his story. It's very sad... but has a relatively good ending. William says Nana is now doing much better at school... but he says he thinks he needs counseling.

Treatment: i'm going to Take william to all the places that certain events occurred and then let him tell us how they unfolded and film them. Where his daughter was abducted from, where the rape happened, where the father of the perpetrator lived, where he found Tshepo, then to joburg court.

I have requested interviews with the FCS officers who will say how amazing william is. And I have requested an interview with NPA.

Extra Budget Items:
Not sure right now, but the make up artist may require us to drop her off and pick her up, or the charge for that is R450.

Script:


In January 2018, in a quiet village in Muldersdrift, Johannesburg – Denzel’s life, and that of his daughter Tuli changed irrevocably.



It was at the most unexpected time too – 10am on a Saturday.







Denzel: I received a call from my wife, telling me that my daughter was kidnapped.



Tuli shots from day 1 on cap camera and justins end of the day

This might come as a shock, but this is not Denzel’s actual name or face.



The law requires us to hide the identities of children who’ve been sexually violated, so we conceal Tuli’s…

REVEAL SHOT IS 00057 – Put’s glasses on him…

CLAIRE LINK 00039

THEREFORE WE ALSO HAVE TO PROTECT AND HIDE DENZEL’S IDENTITY, SO THAT THE PUBLIC DON’T PUT TWO AND TWO TOGETHER, AND THAT’S WHY WE HAVE A MAKE UP ARTIST APPLYING SPECIAL EFFECTS MAKE UP ON HIM.



SUBTITLE

Denzel: I was very very shocked, and I was also crying as a parent, because it was a few hours that my daughter was missing, I was feeling like my daughter was dead.



Show dramatization

Tuli’s abductor was known to the community as a taxi operator – 25-year old Tshepo Moeketsi.



00064 day 2 – justin camera link





THIS IS WHERE TULI WAS HOME WITH HER FRIENDS WHEN TSHEPO APPROACHED IN HIS TAXI, HE STOPPED NEXT TO THE GROUP OF CHILDREN, AND SAID TO HER TO GO BUY HIM A CIGARETTE…WHEN SHE WENT TO THE TUCKSHOP, THAT WHERE HE U TURNED, AND ON HER RETURN THAT’S WHERE TSHEPO SAW HIS OPPORTUNITY, HE NABBED THE CHILD, AND SPED OFF.













As everyone began searching for her, Tshepo had forced Tuli into a secluded veld where he raped the 11 year old girl brutally. Tshepo then discarded the near lifeless child on this deserted stretch of road and callously threw a R20 note at her. Tuli’s injuries were so severe she couldn’t walk.



00076 link

AFTER TSHEPO VIOLENTLY ATTACKED TULI HE JUST LEFT HER THERE, AND SHE DRAGGED HERSELF DOWN THIS HILL, AND MUSTERED THE STRENGTH TO CRAWL ALL THE WAY UP THIS HILL, WITH HER SEVERE INJURIES AND NOT ONE PERSON STOPPED TO HELP HER.



SHOW DAUNTING HILL SHOT

By sheer willpower she pushed her way to safety 2km away and was rushed to hospital. The perpetrators DNA was collected as evidence and sent for testing. She remained in hospital for several days as she needed reconstructive surgery.



Denzel

Denzel: When we were looking at my kid, we were crying, me and my wife, because she couldn’t cope, she couldn’t sleep, she couldn’t do anything.





Denzel says the local police were unhelpful. And it was then he discovered that Tshepo’s father was an influential and wealthy taxi boss.



00059 NEW CLIP – DENZEL

Claire: Did you get a visit from Tshepo’s father at some point?

Denzel: They offered to give me money to drop all the charges.

Claire: Did you accept the money?

Denzel: I didn’t accept the money, because I was thinking of the life of my child.





Denzel’s refusal drove Tshepo into hiding where he evaded capture for the next 8 months.



Undeterred, Denzel’s anger fuelled his determination to bring his daughter’s rapist to justice.



His employer assisted financially with tens of thousands of Rands, and friends helped him to visit neighbouring townships tracking down leads. He spent hours tracing known whereabouts and paid people for information – nothing dimmed his resolve to find the culprit.



Eventually he was pointed in the direction of Madidi – a township near Brits in the Northwest Province. Denzel informed the local police who accompanied him to the house.



new clip denzel

Denzel: When Tshepo found out that there’s people looking for him, then he hid there. To find him, we heard the sound of the pots in the kitchen cupboard.

Claire: Any father in your position would have taken the law into their hands?

Denzel: We couldn’t do that, because we respect the law.





Tshepo was finally arrested and his case was assigned to the specialised police unit that deals with sexual crimes. Sergeant Mpane Mpiko took over.



Female officer 00015 – day 2 justin camera

Sgt Mpiko

Mpiko: There’s other cases that I was investigating whereby he was linked by DNA results, the suspect then alleged these were his girlfriends.





But the sharp officer questioned Tshepo’s version.





Mpiko: If he says they are his girlfriends, why did he sexually abuse them and take them to an open veld, but he didn’t clarify or say the reason why.





Then allegations of corruption began to emerge.



Female officer 00015 – day 2 justin camera

Sgt Mpiko

Mpiko: He was once arrested for the other cases, and then he was released, the reason was not known.

Do we suspect foul play there?

Mpiko: I suspect that the father did play a role.





When Mpiko’s docket was complete, police sergeant Outh-sit-se Saaiman brought it to trial. It was there that allegations of intimidation by Tshepo’s father came to light.



Male cop: Sergeant Saaiman

Saaiman: The father literally you know sent people to the victims houses with money

Claire: And how much money are we talking about here?

Saaiman: The one victim said they were promised fifty thousand each.

Claire: How would you describe the suspects father?

Saaiman: He was powerful, he owned a fleet of taxis. We believed that there were more cases and some of the victims did not come forward.





These allegations have gone unanswered as all attempts to contact Tshepo’s father have been in vain. Both the police and prosecutors say the alleged threats and intimidation made their jobs more difficult. The trial was handed to experienced state prosecutor, Advocate Deborah Zinn.



Zinn

Zinn: There are also police officers who own taxis And they will also not keen to upset the father of this accused.





Zinn knew that her cross-examination would have to expose Tshepo Moeketsi.



Zinn

Zinn: At the onset of the trial it was as if it was a joke to him. Then it becomes arrogant. But as the witnesses testify as it unfolds. And the case mounts against him. He becomes more and more silent.all of a sudden. The accused can't speak up he's lost his voice when he's faced with the contradictions





Prosecutor Zinn found Tuli and her family’s support remarkable.



Zinn

Zinn: I found myself gaining strength from her. She was an inspiration. She was a shining light. She was an excellent witness.





Against all odds Prosecutor Zinn secured convictions on several rape and kidnapping charges relating to 6 of the victims.



Prosecutor Zinn

Zinn: He was sentenced to terms of life imprisonment together with 56 years. And then no application was brought for leave to appeal.



Denzel

Denzel: I feel happy for life in prison, that’s the justice that I was looking for.





University of Johannesburg’s research associate Lisa Vetten wrote a doctoral thesis on South African rape statistics and says the odds of gaining convictions like this are slim.



vetten

Vetten: So we lose about 50 percent of cases at the arrest stage But in terms of how many actually start a trial and result in convictions we talking probably round about seven percent.





Vetten says the data on rape statistics is outdated and inaccuarate, so we actually have no clear idea how South Africa is faring in combatting sexual crimes.



LISA VETTEN

Vetten: At the end of the day that's all the police statistics measure how many women children and men are willing to come to the police and say I have been raped. if we look at this year's statistics that they released. the rape statistics are unverified because the police have not yet taken into account unfounded cases an unfounded case typically means a case where somebody is lying. that's very interesting. How are the police going about determining whether or not somebody is lying?





Vetten would like to see politics set aside and statistics treated as pertinent information.





Vetten: We use them far too much as an indicator. Are the police doing a good job or are they doing a bad job, they need to be depoliticized, there needs to be used as information and data not as political point scoring.





Tuli is now back at school, but despite her receiving extensive counselling, her traumatic past hasn’t been erased by her rapists’ conviction.



Denzel

Denzel: When he was born she was good, she was perfect, she was going to school, she was loving people, also, she was loving me, but after what happened, even today, my daughter, she doesn’t like me like before.



prosecutor CAN WE USE MORE VISUALS OF THE ADVOCATE IN

Zinn: We will do whatever we can to protect you and to see at the end of the day the changes in the victims all of them. It's incredible. It makes it worth it because it gives us courage and it gives us hope. And it helps us to do better and to put in the effort with every case as if it's our first as if we haven't done nothing and to treat each victim with the respect that she deserves.

Zinn Zinn: There are also police officers who own taxis And they will also not keen to upset the father of this accused. Zinn knew that her cross-examination would have to expose Tshepo Moeketsi. Zinn Zinn: At the onset of the trial it was as if it was a joke to him. Then it becomes arrogant. But as the witnesses testify as it unfolds. And the case mounts against him. He becomes more and more silent.all of a sudden. The accused can't speak up he's lost his voice when he's faced with the contradictions Prosecutor Zinn found Tuli and her family’s support remarkable. Zinn Zinn: I found myself gaining strength from her. She was an inspiration. She was a shining light. She was an excellent witness. Against all odds Prosecutor Zinn secured convictions on several rape and kidnapping charges relating to 6 of the victims. Prosecutor Zinn Zinn: He was sentenced to terms of life imprisonment together with 56 years. And then no application was brought for leave to appeal. Denzel Denzel: I feel happy for life in prison, that’s the justice that I was looking for. University of Johannesburg’s research associate Lisa Vetten wrote a doctoral thesis on South African rape statistics and says the odds of gaining convictions like this are slim. vetten Vetten: So we lose about 50 percent of cases at the arrest stage But in terms of how many actually start a trial and result in convictions we talking probably round about seven percent. Vetten says the data on rape statistics is outdated and inaccuarate, so we actually have no clear idea how South Africa is faring in combatting sexual crimes. LISA VETTEN Vetten: At the end of the day that's all the police statistics measure how many women children and men are willing to come to the police and say I have been raped. if we look at this year's statistics that they released. the rape statistics are unverified because the police have not yet taken into account unfounded cases an unfounded case typically means a case where somebody is lying. that's very interesting. How are the police going about determining whether or not somebody is lying? Vetten would like to see politics set aside and statistics treated as pertinent information. Vetten: We use them far too much as an indicator. Are the police doing a good job or are they doing a bad job, they need to be depoliticized, there needs to be used as information and data not as political point scoring. Tuli is now back at school, but despite her receiving extensive counselling, her traumatic past hasn’t been erased by her rapists’ conviction. Denzel Denzel: When he was born she was good, she was perfect, she was going to school, she was loving people, also, she was loving me, but after what happened, even today, my daughter, she doesn’t like me like before. prosecutor CAN WE USE MORE VISUALS OF THE ADVOCATE IN Zinn: We will do whatever we can to protect you and to see at the end of the day the changes in the victims all of them. It's incredible. It makes it worth it because it gives us courage and it gives us hope. And it helps us to do better and to put in the effort with every case as if it's our first as if we haven't done nothing and to treat each victim with the respect that she deserves.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Exclusive: A father refuses to let justice slide after his daughter's rape. He goes after the perpetrator himself. Not only does he catch him but turns out he's a serial rapist.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have the story exclusively. The father will speak, and in a TV first in SA, we are going to hide his identity using make up - a prosthetic nose and beard. This will ensure we meet the legal requirements. Dario has approved of this, as has Luke Lamrecht - in terms of the ethics. SHOULD WE CONFRONT THE FATHER OF THE PERPETRATOR? I'LL LEAVE IT UP TO OFFICE. But he is SUUUUUUPER DANGEROUS. I'm happy to, William is happy to, Police say he's very dangerous, and has made witnesses and others disappear. He is also a convicted murderer. STORY: William is a father who has gone all out to catch the man who raped his daughter. He moved to South Africa from Malawi in 1997 and met his wife, who is South African, they have had two girls, Julia and Ennelise - "Nana" as a nickname. When they lived in Muldersdrift, Nana was 11 years old, when a man in a taxi approached her. He wanted her to buy him a cigarette at the tuckshop. She complied. When she came back, he scooped her up onto his lap, and drove away with her. He took her past Lanseria airport and raped her brutally. The man then dropped her off in the bush, throwing a R20 note at her. Hardly able to walk from the pain, she managed to get to the side of the road where another taxi managed to pick her up and drop her nearby her home. Her mother, and aunt immediately took her to a hospital, where they got a rape kit and J88 form done...and then they went through the painful process of her identifying her rapist and retelling the horror story. She was able to give a very good description, and semen was taken and sent for a DNA test. Then her mother called William, he was beside himself with grief. He couldn't believe this had happened, and he decided that no matter what he would get the man. Based on the description, William managed to track down the man who raped her - Tshepo Moeketsi. Turns out, he was a man well known to the community, not only that, but when they went to the Muldersdrift police station seems that there were several other cases of rape against him. However, he'd not been arrested. William insisted. The next thing, Tshepo's father called. A man also well known in the community - he had murdered a 12 year old boy who stole sweets from his tuckshop... he'd spent several years in jail for that crime. Tshepo's father came to William's house to ask if they could remunerate him (admitting his son was guilty) instead of him laying a charge. William said he must bring Tshepo to his house. But instead Tshepo went into hiding, as William had no intention of taking the bribe. William works as a chef and driver for Anthony Roux. Roux was devastated for William and helped him with the hospital bills, as Nana needed an operation after the ordeal. He also hired a PI to help William find the culprit. But the Muldersdrift police tipped off Tshepo's father, who hid Tshepo when the police raided the family home. And Tshepo remained hidden for the next 8 months. William said he had sleepless nights, taking care of Nana, she was in a bad way. She had counselling which her mother took her to in Krugersdorp. But for a long time she couldn't sit, or go to the loo she was in such pain. She also had nightmares. William said it drove him to obsession. So he decided he would do everything to hunt down Tshepo.
metadata.Summary: Meanwhile, William refused to drop the case, and Tshepo's father sent people to the family's house to threaten them and intimidate them. Roux moved William to a new house in cosmos city away from Muldersdrift as he worried for Williams family's safety. He then decided to help fund William's search for justice, giving him time off and money to go find Tshepo. William began paying informers in the local townships, they would track William's father's vehicle, this lead to several other houses they owned, eventually going to one in a township called Madidi (which is near Brits). There William and two of his friends managed to find someone who knew Tshepo and confirmed Tshepo was staying in his father's house. They went from Tavern to Tavern to Tavern... until finally they found Tshepo... they followed him to his house... there they surprised him and found him hiding in the cupboard. William Tasered him, and it took everything in him to do the right thing. He took him to the police station, and finally Tshepo was arrested. When they got Tshepo's DNA back, turns out there were many rapes he was connected to. 16 woman, and 4 children. These are those that we know of. Over the next year William went to every court hearing, some families were paid R50,000 to drop cases against Tshepo by his father, but William stayed the course - refusing to have his daughter "bought off". He gathered community members and got people to go to the court case - all the time Roux assisted where he could. Finally last week Tuesday 28 July Tshepo, who was found guilty earlier this year, was sentenced to life in prison. I told William about the law requiring us to conceal the identity of the child and family, and he said he and his wife want to speak, they dont need to have their real names, but they want to show their faces - they are adamant that he was able to rape their child because so many stayed silent or were happy to be paid off.
metadata.Further information: There is some footage of the original raid of the police, a shaky cell phone video. But we have pictures of Tshepo's ID, and William can take us everywhere and show us what happened there. I think if we add this to the recent crime statistics, we can actually tell a positive story on a very dark tale. That's my idea - to do re-enactments and go to the places, and Tshepo tell his story. It's very sad... but has a relatively good ending. William says Nana is now doing much better at school... but he says he thinks he needs counseling. Treatment: i'm going to Take william to all the places that certain events occurred and then let him tell us how they unfolded and film them. Where his daughter was abducted from, where the rape happened, where the father of the perpetrator lived, where he found Tshepo, then to joburg court. I have requested interviews with the FCS officers who will say how amazing william is. And I have requested an interview with NPA.
